research_evidence.query: Which ranking objective and sampling implementation reliably improves the official FM?
research_evidence.reason: Cold-start runs repeatedly proposed BPR but implementation quality varied sharply.
research_evidence.summary: Use vectorized same-user BPR, not all-batch quadratic pairing. Build per-user positive blocks and negative pools only for users with both classes; use one sampled same-user negative per positive per epoch; align positive and negative arrays by user block; return safely when no eligible pairs; the FM global bias cancels. The exact loss is L=mean(softplus(-(z_pos-z_neg))). With diff=z_pos-z_neg, use g_pos=(sigmoid(diff)-1)/pair_count and g_neg=-g_pos. At diff=0, g_pos must equal -0.5/pair_count, never +0.5/pair_count; a one-step sanity check must increase z_pos-z_neg. At k=16, lr=0.001, one negative, the five-seed official-validation primary changed from 0.601500738 ± 0.000481897 for pointwise FM to 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR. Treat the mechanism and implementation invariants as the prior; rerun it inside the Agent harness rather than assuming the measured delta transfers exactly.

It edits only the features block and adds the seven selected, low-cardinality, static pre-impression user profile fields to the globally offset categorical matrix returned by SO.build_features. The proposal therefore creates legal user-candidate interaction terms while preserving the validated ranking objective. It is a direct catalogued refinement rather than an unsupported custom reconstruction.

proposal.hypothesis: Doubling the training mass of tab-6 impressions will produce a tab-6-specialized ordering that improves the selected parent's largest diagnosed residual slice and yields positive marginal contribution to the heterogeneous portfolio without materially degrading dominant tab=1 traffic.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit only the train block. Before calling SO.train, read the legal pre-impression tab array from splits['train'].tab, select indices in the supplied train_idx whose tab equals 6, concatenate one additional copy of those indices with train_idx, sort the resulting index array, and pass that expanded index array to SO.train. Keep Xs, target construction, objective, all HP values, and prediction unchanged. This deterministic row replication gives tab-6 observations approximately double training mass in both the pairwise and censored-watch training paths without exposing evaluation labels or adding tab as a post-feedback feature.
proposal.justification: The large, repeated tab-6 deficit identifies a concrete residual segment rather than motivating an undirected scalar tune. Deterministically replicating only train tab-6 rows connects that diagnostic to the existing executable BPR/auxiliary training consumer and should shift learned item/context interactions toward this segment. Because the portfolio already contains strong but correlated generalists, a bounded specialist can succeed through complementary ordering even if its standalone average gain is modest.
proposal.observation: The supplied portfolio diagnostic reports w001's largest tab disadvantage at portfolio_diagnostics.members[w001].slice_specialization.member_disadvantages for tab=6 with delta_primary=-0.036711203406393667 over 5,170 rows and 2,212 users. The last measured candidate also had directional_feedback.tab for tab=6 equal to -0.011354706892621413 versus the incumbent, while changes on most other tabs were near zero.
proposal.research_nonuse_reason: The exact tab-6 residual diagnostics and the visible train_idx consumer directly motivate this reward reweighting. E003 only rejects increasing bpr_censored_watch aux_weight from 0.1 to 0.2 and supplies no evidence for tab-conditional weighting; this proposal leaves aux_weight unchanged.

matches.hypothesis: A leakage-safe censored watch-time auxiliary will teach duration-sensitive item-quality interactions not fully captured by the four sparse engagement heads, yielding complementary within-user ordering and positive marginal contribution to the heterogeneous portfolio.
matches.implementation_plan: Add one censored watch-time regression head to a visible reproduction of the w002 DeepFM while leaving native long_view as the main pointwise label and retaining its four engagement heads. In the target block, call DV.watch_ratio() on train only, combine valid ratios with splits['train'].duration_ms to derive played_ms, and construct scaled log targets log1p(played_ms)/12 and log-duration bounds log1p(duration_ms)/12. Mark completed observations where valid and played_ms>=duration_ms; exclude invalid ratios and zero-duration rows from this auxiliary loss. In the model block, attach a scalar watch head to the same shared FM/deep representation used by the ranking and engagement heads. In the train block, use exact regression residual loss for incomplete plays and a one-sided lower-bound hinge for completed plays that becomes zero once the prediction reaches the log-duration bound. Add this auxiliary at fixed weight 0.2, with all other architecture and optimization settings held to the parent values.

selection_rationale: Candidate 0 is the only viable candidate. It directly targets a large, repeated tab=6 residual deficit using a legal pre-impression field and an executable SO.train index path. The change is structural rather than scalar-only, preserves the parent’s features, targets, hyperparameters, and prediction logic, and has a clear error-diversifier role under the active portfolio reward. Its deterministic one-copy replication rule is attributable and falsifiable through the expanded row count, changed prediction hashes, tab=6 slice movement, and trusted marginal portfolio primary. No exact matching negative result is reported: the cited negative result concerns an aux_weight transition that this candidate explicitly leaves unchanged. Although there is risk from the much larger tab=1 segment and from noisy tab=6 examples, the diagnostic basis and implementation connection make this more credible than an unsupported mechanism change; there are no other viable candidates to compare.
